item.title: 7 ways to Create Table in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Learn 7 ways to create tables in Oracle SQL, including examples and tips. Discover using the CREATE TABLE statement, the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement, the CREATE TABLE LIKE statement, the CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE statement, the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement, the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement, and the CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE statement.

Summary of Create table in Oracle: Creating tables in Oracle SQL is a fundamental task in database management. There are several ways to create tables in Oracle, including the CREATE TABLE statement, the CREATE TABLE AS SELECT statement, the CREATE TABLE LIKE statement, the CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE statement, the CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW statement, the CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE statement, and the CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE statement.

item.title: 7 Alternative to CONCAT_Ws in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Learn about the different ways to concatenate strings in Oracle, including the CONCAT and CONCAT_WS in Oracle functions and the “||” operator . Discover how to concatenate strings with and without separators, and see examples using the JustLee Book Database .

Summary of tutorial: This tutorial covers 7 different ways to concatenate strings in Oracle. It includes an introduction to concatenation in Oracle, and covers the CONCAT function and “||” operator, as well as other methods. For each method, SQL query syntax and examples are provided using the JustLee Book Database .

item.title: Drop Table IF EXISTS in Oracle - Alternative Solutions
item.description:
Learn about the best ways to drop table if exists in Oracle if it exists. Oracle does not support the “IF EXISTS” clause, but there are several alternative solutions to achieve the same result. Find out how to use exception handling, the “WHENEVER SQLERROR ” command, and more to drop a table in Oracle if it exists.

Oracle does not support the “IF EXISTS” clause

Summary: In this tutorial, we will discuss various ways to drop a table in Oracle if it exists. Oracle does not support the “IF EXISTS” clause, but there are several alternative solutions that can be used to achieve the same result. We will explore the use of exception handling, the EXECUTE IMMEDIATE command, the “WHENEVER SQLERROR” command, and more to drop a table in Oracle if it exists.

item.title: How to generate insert statements from existing table in Oracle SQL
item.description:
This tutorial will help you to learn how to generate insert statements from existing table in Oracle SQL. Learn the different ways to do this and see examples using the JustLee book database .

**Summary of tutorial post:**In this tutorial, we will discuss the various ways to generate insert statements from an existing table in Oracle SQL. We will provide examples using the JustLee book database to show how to generate insert statements using the SELECT statement, the INSERT INTO SELECT statement, and the CTAS ( CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) statement. We will also discuss some frequently asked questions about generating insert statements in Oracle SQL.

item.title: How to use Union in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Learn how to use the Union operator in Oracle SQL to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements. This tutorial includes examples and tips for using Union in Oracle SQL with the JustLee book database and a school sample database.

Introduction to Union in Oracle SQL:

The Union operator in Oracle SQL is used to combine the results of two or more SELECT statements into a single result set. This can be useful when you need to combine data from multiple tables or when you want to return a single result set that includes the results of multiple SELECT statements.

item.title: What Is Oracle? Intro to Oracle Databases
item.description:
Oracle Database is a powerful, multi-model relational database management system (RDBMS) developed by Oracle Corporation. Designed for enterprise-scale applications, Oracle Database provides a comprehensive solution for data management, offering high performance, scalability, and reliability.

First released in 1979, Oracle has evolved to support both structured and unstructured data, becoming a top choice for businesses requiring robust database solutions.

Key Features of Oracle Database

  1. High Availability
    Oracle Database includes features like Real Application Clusters (RAC) and Data Guard to ensure minimal downtime and maximum uptime.

item.title: How to ALTER TABLE in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Meta Description of ALTER TABLE in Oracle:
ALTER TABLE is a DDL (Data Definition Language) statement in Oracle that allows you to modify the structure of an existing table. This includes adding, modifying, or dropping columns, constraints, and indexes. In this tutorial, we will learn the syntax and various features of the ALTER TABLE statement and provide examples of how to use it in Oracle.

Summary of ALTER TABLE in Oracle:

ALTER TABLE is a DDL statement used to modify the structure of an existing table in Oracle
It can be used to add, modify, or drop columns, constraints, and indexes
The syntax for ALTER TABLE includes the table name, the action to be performed (ADD, MODIFY, DROP), and the specification of the column, constraint, or index being modified
ALTER TABLE has several options and features, including RENAME , ENABLE/DISABLE, and VALIDATE/NOVALIDATE

item.title: How to create CHECK constraint on date in Oracle SQL
item.description:
In this tutorial, we will learn about the CHECK constraint on date in Oracle SQL, including its syntax, types, and examples using the JustLee book database.

Summary of CHECK constraint on date: A CHECK constraint is used to enforce a condition on one or more columns of a table in SQL. The CHECK constraint on date is used to ensure that the value in a date column meets certain conditions, such as being a valid date or falling within a specified range. This tutorial will cover the syntax, types, and examples of using the CHECK constraint on date in Oracle SQL .

item.title: How to Create Function in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Learn how to create a function in Oracle using the CREATE FUNCTION statement. This tutorial includes syntax, features, and examples using the JustLee book database.

Summary of create function in Oracle: A function in Oracle is a stored program that can accept input parameters and return a value or multiple values. In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a function in Oracle using the CREATE FUNCTION statement. We will also explore the syntax and features of the create function statement, as well as provide examples using the JustLee book database.

item.title: How to Create Custom Datatype in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Summary of create custom datatype in Oracle: In this tutorial, we will learn how to create a custom datatype in Oracle using the CREATE TYPE statement. We will also cover the syntax and features of custom datatypes, and provide query examples using the JustLee Book database.  

Introduction to create custom datatype in Oracle:

In Oracle, a datatype is a set of attributes that describe the type of data that a column or variable can hold. Oracle provides a variety of predefined datatypes, such as NUMBER , VARCHAR2, and DATE . However, sometimes you may need to store data in a way that is not supported by the predefined datatypes. In these cases, you can create a custom datatype using the CREATE TYPE statement.

item.title: How to use datatypes in Oracle SQL
item.description:
Meta Description of use datatypes in Oracle: In this tutorial, we will learn how to use datatypes in Oracle to specify the type of data that a column or variable can hold. We will cover the syntax and features of Oracle’s predefined datatypes, and provide query examples using the JustLee Book database and a school sample database.

Summary of use datatypes in Oracle:

Introduction to use datatypes in Oracle:

In Oracle, a datatype is a set of attributes that describe the type of data that a column or variable can hold. Oracle provides a variety of predefined datatypes, such as NUMBER, VARCHAR2, and DATE. By specifying a datatype for a column or variable, you ensure that the data stored in it is consistent and meets the requirements of your application.
